purpose: Bacitracin is an antibiotic ointment used on the skin to prevent or treat minor bacterial infections in small cuts, scrapes, and burns. It helps keep wounds clean and free from infection while they heal. It is for external use on the skin only and is not meant to be swallowed.
how_it_works: Bacitracin works by blocking bacteria from building the protective outer wall they need to survive. Without this wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. This stops the infection from spreading and allows your skin to heal naturally.
common_side_effects: Most people do not have serious side effects when using bacitracin on the skin. Some people may notice mild redness, itching, or a rash at the spot where it is applied. In rare cases, some people can have an allergic reaction, which may cause more significant redness, swelling, or hives.
warnings: Stop using bacitracin and contact your doctor right away if you notice signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, or severe rash. Do not use it in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on large areas of skin unless your doctor tells you to. Do not use it for more than 1 week without checking with your doctor. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to any antibiotics before using this product.
typical_dosing: For most minor skin wounds, apply a small amount of bacitracin ointment to the affected area 1 to 3 times per day. Clean the area gently before applying. You can cover it with a bandage if needed. Use only enough to lightly coat the wound — a little goes a long way.
